name: יְחִיאֵל
summary: Eleven men, nearly all Levites and men of the house of God: a Levite singer with lyres when David brought up the ark (1Ch 15:18, 20; 16:5); a Gershonite, head of the house of Ladan, over the treasuries of the house of Yahweh (1Ch 23:8; 29:8; also called יְחִיאֵלִי, 1Ch 26:21–22); a companion of the king's sons (1Ch 27:32); a son of Jehoshaphat (2Ch 21:2); a Hemanite who cleansed the house under Hezekiah (2Ch 29:14) and an overseer of the offerings (2Ch 31:13); a ruler of the house of God under Josiah (2Ch 35:8); and men of the return, among them the father of Shecaniah, who confessed the marriages with foreign women (Ezr 10:2), and men who had married them (Ezr 10:21, 26). The name is the imperfect of חָיָה with אֵל: “may God live” or “God lives”, the form of the acclamation יְחִי הַמֶּלֶךְ, “may the king live” (1Sa 10:24).

evidence.note: וִיחִיאֵל among the Levites of the second rank appointed as singers.
“The sons of Ladan: the chief יְחִיאֵל, and Zetham and Joel.”
The same family as יְחִיאֵלִי: “the sons of Jehieli, Zetham and Joel his brother, over the treasuries of the house of Yahweh.”
The stones were given to the treasury “by the hand of יְחִיאֵל the Gershonite”.
יְחִי הַמֶּלֶךְ, “may the king live”: the same form of the verb the name is built on.

note: Takes h.cd.ak (the name, 14 tokens) and h.cd.al (the patronymic form יְחִיאֵלִי, 2 tokens), which TIPNR lists as a form of Jehiel@1Ch.6.20. The name is not explained in scripture; “may God live” takes יְחִי as jussive, as in the acclamation, and “God lives” as indicative; both are the root's sense. TIPNR names the Hemanite of 2Ch 29:14 Jehuel (the ketiv there is יחואל) though the text's word is יְחִיאֵל. The people's identifications are TIPNR's. BDB's cross-reference keys h.ba.ac and j.be.ak have no tokens and are not claimed.
